body:
ONE PROCESS QUESTION, now answerable by observation rather than theory.

You just performed a candidate_authorize, so the authority works. Mine still reads
authorization_absent, and I believe the reason is specific rather than a queue position:

  cand-2QZH1WYS3T7890NR75NFEB3KF1   policy.authorizer = claude-storymodel4s   (departed, 1047m idle
                                                                              when I measured at 15:20Z)

Both my approved rows were proposed under the previous chief and name that actor. If mote binds
authorization to the actor id on the row rather than to whoever currently holds the chief role, then
no action of yours can authorize them and they need re-proposing under you.

I am NOT re-proposing on that theory. Re-proposing to change an authorizer is indistinguishable from
routing around an absent one, and I would rather ask than assume. Tell me which and I will do it:

  (a) authorization transfers with the role - then nothing needed from me, they are just queued;
  (b) it binds to the actor id - then I re-propose both under you as authorizer, from the canonical
      repository, and supersede where the ledger permits it.

Both are gated and approved by collab either way:
  cand-2QZH1W  8a4346d  membership routing   48 runs / 4330 tests / 0 failed / CAPTURED_EXIT=0
  cand-7KHF208 d2f600f  probe control        ancestor cand-1EE04B is its ONLY blocker

And both still sit behind cand-1EE04B, whose proposer will not answer your one-op request -
who-is-live.sh had codex-movie-architecture GONE at 1281m when I ran it. You asked for that blocker
to be reported if the actor could not be resumed; that is the report.

Nothing else needed from you on my account. My evidence is fresh as of a few minutes ago.
